about.title: Needles Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: A fall on a wet floor, broken step, or uneven pavement can happen at a gas station off Interstate 40, a motel near Needles Highway, or a shop along Route 95. These properties see steady traffic from travelers and locals alike, and when an owner or manager ignores a hazard, the person who slips pays the price. California law asks whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and failed to fix it or warn visitors. That's why documenting the scene matters so much, photos of the hazard, witness names, and a written request for surveillance footage before it's erased. Needles businesses often rely on cameras that overwrite within days or weeks. San Bernardino County's rules and a strict two-year filing window (shorter if a government entity is involved) make early action valuable. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself, but we can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who reviews these details and works on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Notice and Evidence

items.title: Notice Is the Heart of the Case
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that speak to that knowledge.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many stores and motels in Needles overwrite security video within days. Prompt legal help can mean a preservation letter goes out before that evidence is lost.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Recovery
items.desc: Even if you were partly distracted or wearing certain shoes, California's pure comparative fault rule still lets you pursue compensation, just adjusted for your share of responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Needles?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government-owned property is involved, such as a public building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early administrative claim. An attorney can confirm which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame, though your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of fault. This applies whether the fall happened at a truck stop off I-40 or a store along Needles Highway. An independent attorney can help assess how fault might be divided in your case.

items.question: Why does surveillance video matter so much for my claim?
items.answer: Many businesses in Needles, including those near the I-40 corridor, only retain camera footage for a short window before it's automatically deleted. That footage can show exactly how long a hazard was present, which speaks directly to whether the owner had notice. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can make a real difference.
